artists.biography:
The Beautiful South was an English pop group formed at the end of the 1980s by two former members of Hull group The Housemartins, Paul Heaton and Dave Hemingway. Other members were Sean Welch (bass), Dave Stead (drums) and Dave Rotheray (guitar) and a succession of female vocalists - Briana Corrigan, Jacqui Abbott and Alison Wheeler.
The group broke up in January 2007, claiming the split was due to "musical similarities", having sold around 15,000,000 records worldwide. In January 2009, it was announced that the former members Dave Hemingway, Alison Wheeler, and Dave Stead would reform under the name "New Beautiful South" which was later changed to "The South".

perplexity.description:
Released in March 1992 by Go! Discs, 0898 Beautiful South is the third studio album by the English pop-rock band The Beautiful South. The album features a more muscular and occasionally sombre sound compared to their earlier work, while retaining the band's signature blend of melodic arrangements and lyricist Paul Heaton's characteristically witty, bittersweet songwriting. Produced by Jon Kelly at AIR Studios in London, the record showcases the group's evolving musical maturity, balancing lush instrumentation with introspective themes.

Musically, 0898 Beautiful South sits at the intersection of rock and pop, with sophisticated arrangements and a subtle, sometimes melancholic edge. The album produced four singles—"Old Red Eyes Is Back," "We Are Each Other," "Bell Bottomed Tear," and "36D"—two of which were released ahead of the album. It reached number 4 on the UK Albums Chart, a slight dip from their previous two albums, which both peaked at number 2; the record company attributed this to the controversial album cover. Despite this, the album remained on the chart for 17 weeks and was certified Gold by the BPI for sales exceeding 200,000 copies, affirming its place as a significant release in the band's discography.
